title: D'oh! Operation Flagship
summary: Josh and Chuck (transcribed as "iHeart Intro" for Chuck) examine Operation Flagship, a 1985 US Marshals Service sting that lured fugitives to a fake Redskins football game with promised free tickets. The episode traces the Marshals' 1980s run of cutesy fugitive stings (Fugitive Investigative Strike Team, or FIST, Mister Zip, Punos Airlines, the Brooklyn Bridge Delivery Service, and the Culture Club giveaway in Hartford, Connecticut). It then details the Flagship setup: the fake TV station, the backwards-named signatories, the rehearsals, the cheerleader pat-downs, the "confirmed winner" and "double winner" name tags, the arrests, and the media coverage. It also covers the costs and arrest counts, the wrong-man error with Charles Watkins Sr. versus his son, which was uncovered by a CBS News producer and reported on the Criminal podcast, and the Marshals' later shift away from these stings. Segments also include tangents on football, M. Night Shyamalan films, The Simpsons, and a listener email about breakfast foods.
topics: Boy George Culture Club fake TV giveaway
fake prize scams used by police

segments.title: Opening banter and cutesy law enforcement names
segments.summary: The hosts introduce the episode's theme: a 1985 law enforcement sting with cutesy names and acronyms.

segments.title: US Marshals Service history and role
segments.summary: Overview of the US Marshals Service, founded in 1789, its historical roles, and its modern duties including witness protection, prisoner transport, and fugitive investigations since 1979.

segments.title: Fugitive Investigative Strike Team and Mister Zip
segments.summary: The Marshals launched FIST in 1981 to round up fugitives in large batches through sting operations, rather than one at a time. Mister Zip used Marshals dressed as mail carriers to arrest fugitives at their doors.

segments.title: Punos Airlines sting
segments.summary: A fake sweepstakes for a free Bahamas trip sent through a fake airline named Punos, which means fist in Spanish. Fourteen fugitives fell for it and most were arrested in the limo; one reached a fake ticket counter at Miami International.

segments.title: Other 1984 and 1985 stings
segments.summary: The hosts describe a job-offer sting called the Prior Offenders Employment Opportunity Program, and a Brooklyn Bridge Delivery Service package scam run by Robert Leshorn, which tailored fake packages to each fugitive's alleged crime.

segments.title: Hartford Boy George Culture Club sting
segments.summary: A fake TV station in Hartford, Connecticut offered concert tickets to Culture Club, with dinner, a limo ride and a photo shoot. About 3,200 arrests came from this sting, and it is described as the largest fugitive round-up in American history.

segments.title: Break
segments.summary: Mid-episode break.

segments.title: Origins of Operation Flagship and Redskins football
segments.summary: Howard Sephir proposed the idea at a Christmas party, and Robert Leshorn suggested Redskins football tickets. The hosts discuss the 1985 Redskins season and the December 15, 1985 game against the Bengals, with a tangent on Joe Theismann's leg injury.

segments.title: Fake TV station, cover letters, and backwards names
segments.summary: The fake station was a rock music TV station called WRC Video. The prize letters were signed by station manager Iam Debt Naw, read backwards as I am wanted, and the business manager Marcus Kran was read as Narc. About 3,000 letters went out and roughly 160 people RSVP'd, with a Super Bowl ticket drawing added as a distraction.

segments.title: Rehearsals and undercover staffing
segments.summary: Three dress rehearsals were held. About 166 agents, all disguised as staff and guests, including cheerleaders who hugged and patted down guests, were brought in from out of state so fugitives wouldn't recognize them. The San Diego Chicken was an armed cop.

segments.title: Attempts to settle the crowd and the risks
segments.summary: The hosts discuss the Marshals' concern about dangerous fugitives, including Charles Watkins, a murderer who had escaped from prison in a fake guard uniform. Robert Leshorn's remarks about smiling at bandits are noted.

segments.title: The day of the sting at the Washington Convention Center
segments.summary: On December 15, 1985, guests checked in and received name tags reading confirmed winner or double winner. Fifteen to twenty winners were taken at a time into conference rooms, where emcee Louis McKinney announced the arrests and SWAT officers entered.

segments.title: Plus-ones and the Beach Boys coincidence
segments.summary: The hosts discuss the uninvited plus-ones who were left behind, and Josh describes a coincidence involving the Beach Boys Smile album. An attorney from a local TV station who had the broadcast rights showed up and was removed.

segments.title: Media coverage, arrest counts, and cost
segments.summary: Journalists from the LA Times, CBS News, and the Washington Post covered the event. Arrest counts vary between 101 and 144. The operation cost about $22,100, roughly $218 per arrest. Marshals chief Stanley Morris called it a safe, clean, and creative way to make arrests.

segments.title: Wrong man and the Criminal podcast investigation
segments.summary: Charles Watkins, the top ten fugitive, was arrested, but he was actually the father, Charles Watkins Sr., and the actual fugitive was his son. CBS News producer Alan Goldberg reviewed footage and questioned the operation. The Criminal podcast covered this in a December 2024 episode. The target Lloyd Golden was wanted for drug sales, not armed robbery.

segments.title: Aftermath and the end of the stings
segments.summary: The hosts say the Flagship sting marked the beginning of the end for these stings. Operation North Star captured over 3,000 violent fugitives last year without such scams. The Marshals stopped the Christmas party rum punch in 1986.

segments.title: Pop culture references to the sting
segments.summary: The Flagship sting inspired the opening scene of Sea of Love, and the Mister Zip approach appears in other movies. The Simpsons also featured a similar sting in which Homer falls for a free boat scam.

segments.title: Tangent on M. Night Shyamalan films
segments.summary: The hosts discuss M. Night Shyamalan's films, including Trap, Signs, The Sixth Sense, Unbreakable, Split, Knock at the Cabin, and the series Servant.

segments.title: The Simpsons boat scam and the Marshal Museum
segments.summary: The hosts discuss a Simpsons episode in which Homer falls for a free motorboat scam, and Louis McKinney's top hat is on display at the US Marshals Museum in Fort Smith, Arkansas.

segments.title: Listener mail on breakfast as dessert
segments.summary: A listener writes about breakfast foods being dessert, prompting a discussion of pie, pancakes, French toast, and cereal.

segments.title: Sign-off
segments.summary: The hosts invite emails and sign off, noting the show is a production of iHeartRadio.
